description: LogEntry.hlc_timestamp is u64 (wall milliseconds only). The HlcTimestamp struct has three components: wall_ms, logical counter, and node_id. By storing only wall_ms, two entries from different nodes with identical wall clock values are not causal-ordered correctly via the CRDT merge — the logical counter tie-break is lost. This means the CRDT can fail to total-order concurrent events correctly when clocks happen to agree. Either store the full HlcTimestamp or document that only wall_ms is used for CRDT ordering and explain why precision loss is acceptable.
notes: Fix deferred by coordinator. Full HLC type change requires: (1) change LogEntry.hlc_timestamp from u64 to HlcTimestamp across types.rs, canonical.rs, verify.rs, sqlite_storage.rs; (2) add hlc_logical INTEGER and hlc_node_id BLOB columns to log_entries table via new migration files for both SQLite and PostgreSQL; (3) update storage_tests.rs and all callers. No existing data to migrate (greenfield). Cannot proceed without coordinator approval due to scope of cross-file changes triggering build failures during partial edit.
title: core: LogEntry hlc_timestamp stores wall-ms only, losing logical and node_id components
